7.text: On the Pacific side, these “spirits” are usually called reˊkkeñɪt (sing.

8.text: reˊkkeñ), while in the Kolyma country a reˊkkeñ is a monster with a bear’s

9.text: body and very large ears. I obtained several curious details about the

10.text: supposed ways of the reˊkkeñ tribe. They cannot fly. Even when pursued

11.text: by a shaman, they only dive underground, making the earth near them

12.text: soften and give way like water. They have red canoes, in which they

13.text: ascend even the shallowest waters, also large skin boats with crews of eight

14.text: oarsmen and a boat-master (aᵋtw-eˊrmečɪn), after the manner of men. When

15.text: hunting from these boats, they lay their nets for men, who are their only

16.text: game. Their houses are underground dwellings. Their kettles are made of

17.text: grass. Their fire is snow-white in the day-time and blood-red in the evening,

18.text: when it may be seen in the west after sunset.

19.text: The outward appearance of the reˊkkeñɪt and of their reindeer and dogs

20.text: is unlike that of man and his animals. It is “of different form” (aˊlvam-vaˊlɪn).

21.text: Some of them have only one eye, in their foreheads, and long braided hair.

22.text: They wear loose garments with very long sleeves trailing on the ground,

23.text: while their hands are thrust out through openings in the middle. These

24.text: latter details are repeated in the description of other supernatural beings.

26.text: containing sparks of fire. The women are very stout, and have long loose
